title: Vikarna speaks for her
hookLine: Bhima answers with fire, Arjuna holds him back, and Vikarna, a Kaurava, answers with reasons
carry: dharma comes before your own side
tomorrow: What happens when they pull at her sari?
last: AS THE FOOD, SO THE MIND.

cards: Two voices break the silence, and they break it in opposite directions. First Bhima. He has watched his eldest brother stake him, lose him, and then lose Draupadi, and his anger has nowhere to go.

In the telling, he turns it on Yudhishthira himself. Then someone nobody expects speaks up, a young man from the other side of the family. Two answers to Draupadi's question: one made of fury, one made of reasons.

teach.b: Bhima's words are shocking. Gamblers, he says, don't stake even the women kept in their houses. Then: Sahadeva, bring fire, and I'll burn this brother's arms.
It's the rage of someone who loves his brother and can't bear what he's done. Arjuna stops him: our enemies want exactly this, to see us turn on our eldest. And Bhima holds back.
He's one of Duryodhana's own brothers, a Kaurava, and he stands up in his family's hall and says: answer her. Nobody does.

teach.h: HIS REASONS: SHE WAS NOT WON.
teach.b: So he answers it himself, with reasons. Kings, he says, are prone to certain vices: hunting, drinking, dice, and too much pleasure. A man in their grip acts without judgment.

Yudhishthira staked Draupadi in the grip of the game, at Shakuni's prompting, after he had already lost himself. And she's the wife of all five brothers, not his alone. For these reasons, Vikarna says, she was not won.
The hall erupts, cheering him and blaming Shakuni.

teach.h: NOT AN ELDER, NOT A PANDAVA.
teach.b: Notice who gave the answer: not an elder, not a Pandava, but a younger brother of the winning side. That's a real Hindu teaching, and the epics keep coming back to it.
Dharma isn't loyalty to your own team. It binds you even against your own family.
The tradition honors the ones who said so: Vikarna here, and in the Ramayana, Vibhishana, who told his own brother Ravana to give Sita back.
And see how Vikarna does it: not with Bhima's fire, but with reasons, out loud, in his own family's hall.

how: Vikarna is remembered in retellings as the Kaurava who spoke for Draupadi, held up beside Vibhishana as one who put dharma before his own side; Arjuna's restraint of Bhima is told as the brothers refusing to turn on each other.

o: a question Vikarna answers with reasons
a vow Bhima makes against his eldest brother
a riddle Vidura used to warn the brothers

s: Vikarna was one of the Pandava brothers
he was a Kaurava, one of Duryodhana's own brothers.
Arjuna held Bhima back from turning on Yudhishthira
he said their enemies wanted exactly that.
in Hindu teaching, loyalty to your side always comes before dharma
the epics honor Vikarna and Vibhishana for putting dharma before their own family.

games.q: you're Vikarna. your brothers have won the game. Draupadi asks if she was won, and you know the answer goes against your side. what fits dharma?
o: give your reasons out loud: she was not won.
shout at Shakuni and storm out.
games.why: Vikarna stood in his own family's hall and gave reasons she was not won: dharma before his own side, said with reasons, not fire.

practice: Think of a place where you belong to a side: a family, a team, a friend group. Is there one true thing your side would rather nobody said? Don't say it yet.
Shape it the way Vikarna did, a reason instead of a shout. Many Hindus make a sankalpa, a small resolve, before their home shrine.
If you pray, make yours there and ask for courage; if you don't, write the sentence down and keep it.

wordCard.voice: Draupadi's question. Bhima answers with fire, Arjuna holds him back, and Vikarna, a Kaurava, answers with reasons: she was not won.

orig.note: Sanskrit vyasana: a vice or ruinous habit; Vikarna names the vices that cloud a king's judgment.

carryVoice: Your line: dharma comes before your own side. Vikarna said it in his own family's hall. Day seven hundred seventy-two, done.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Sabha Parva, Dyuta Parva (Bhima's anger at Yudhishthira and call for fire; Arjuna's restraint; Vikarna's speech on the four vices of kings, the order of the stakes and Draupadi as wife of all five; the assembly's applause)
Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (Vibhishana counsels Ravana to return Sita, is rejected, and goes over to Rama)
